chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who said, 'The first slave I own is free,' and then he died leaving seven slaves in total, he said: 'Cast lots among them, and the one whose lot is drawn is freed.'
ai.seo_question: How is the first slave determined for emancipation when a master dies with multiple slaves?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of resolving ambiguity in conditional emancipation (itik) when the specific identity of the 'first' acquired slave is unknown at the time of death. By prescribing the casting of lots (qur'a), the Imam establishes a fair, divinely-sanctioned method to determine which of the multiple slaves fulfills the master's intent, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of resolving doubt through equitable means. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of 'Al-Itq' within Tahdhib al-Ahkam, illustrating the practical application of prophetic tradition in commercial and familial legal matters.
